claim.pdf_says: PDF page 390 (printed 360) ends syntax rule 14 with: "c)  If the literal is national, 'PICTURE N(length)'" and nothing further. PDF page 391 (printed 361) then opens with a SEPARATE paragraph, set at the subrule indent and NOT lettered: "where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals." followed by "15) If BLANK WHEN ZERO or JUSTIFIED is specified, ...".
claim.markdown_says: c) If the literal is national, 'PICTURE N(length)' where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals.
claim.why_it_matters: The 'where length is ...' sentence is the closing definition for ALL THREE implied PICTURE strings of syntax rule 14 (X(length), 1(length), N(length)). Splicing it onto the tail of subrule c) makes it read as if 'length' were defined only for the national case, leaving 'length' undefined for the alphanumeric and boolean subrules. The transcription itself renders the identical construct correctly at 13.16.3 syntax rule 9 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 16953), where the same sentence stands as its own indented paragraph after subrule c), which confirms the p390 rendering is the defect and not the convention.

verdict.reasoning:
INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED on both rendered pages at 300 dpi, with pixel measurements rather than eyeballing.

(1) PDF p390 (printed 360, 13.15.3 Syntax rules): the page's last body line is 'c)  If the literal is national, 'PICTURE N(length)'' at y=2865-2906. Nothing follows before the page number '360' at y=3111. The claimed sentence is genuinely absent from p390.

(2) PDF p391 (printed 361): the first body line, y=388-429, is exactly 'where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals.' It is a standalone paragraph; the next paragraph is '15) If BLANK WHEN ZERO or JUSTIFIED is specified, a COLUMN clause shall also be specified.' Both quotes in the claim are verbatim-accurate.

(3) It is a SEPARATE PARAGRAPH, not a wrap of subrule c). Two independent proofs. (a) Column-width proof: on p390 the c) line ends at x=1244 while the text column runs to x=2285 -- roughly 1040 px (~45 characters) of blank line was left unused. Text belonging to subrule c) would have flowed onto that same line; the typesetter instead broke to a new paragraph on the next page. (b) Indent proof: p391 uses mirrored margins shifted +70 px from p390 (rule numbers 267->337, hanging body 340->410, subrule text 413->483). 'where length' starts at x=407, i.e. the hanging-body / subrule-letter level (410), and is clearly OUTDENTED from the subrule-text level (483) where a continuation of c) would sit. It also carries no letter marker -- the first glyphs are the word 'where'.

(4) The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 16769 concatenates the sentence onto subrule c) with a single space, so 'length' is left undefined for subrules a) (alphanumeric) and b) (boolean). This is a semantic loss for two of the three implied-PICTURE cases, not page-break furniture: the paragraph's scope is narrowed from 'all three subrules' to 'the national subrule only'.

(5) The claim's control case holds and is in fact stronger than stated. The transcription renders the identical construct CORRECTLY in TWO other places: 13.16.3 SR 9 (line 16953, data description entry) and 13.17.3 SR 10 (line 17251, screen description entry) -- both keep 'where length is ...' as its own paragraph after subrule c). Only the 13.15.3 SR 14 instance at line 16769 is spliced. The transcription's own convention therefore identifies p390 as the defect.

(6) Refutation attempts that FAILED: the text is not merely reflowed (it is on the wrong logical parent, and the p390 line had ample room had it belonged there); it is not duplicated or lost (grep finds exactly three occurrences repo-wide, all accounted for); the markdown is not misquoted (line 16769 matches character-for-character); page-391.md correctly omits it, so this is a genuine relocation across the page boundary rather than a rendering artifact of the page split.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed, with one refinement to the claim's typographic description. On PDF p391 the paragraph 'where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals.' is set at x=407, which is the SUBRULE-LETTER / rule-14 hanging-body indent -- it is outdented from the subrule TEXT indent (x=483 on that page's margins) where a continuation of subrule c) would sit, and it carries no letter marker. So it is not merely 'at the subrule indent'; it is a hanging closing paragraph of syntax rule 14 as a whole, which strengthens rather than weakens the claim that it governs all three implied PICTURE strings. Fix: in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, split line 16769 so that 13.15.3 syntax rule 14 reads c) If the literal is national, 'PICTURE N(length)' where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals. matching the already-correct rendering at 13.16.3 SR 9 (line 16953) and 13.17.3 SR 10 (line 17251). The standalone sentence belongs to the p390 rule-14 block even though the PDF prints it at the top of p391, so it should be placed before the anchor.
